title: Nim — 10 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
Nim — 10 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the machine. 10 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 4 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 38 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 10. Most binding: xorN (7), N (5), isLost (4), grundy1 (2).

2 · Imports. Built on: fnv.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 file(s): src/proof/nim.lean, src/proof/fnv.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 10 sealed receipts fold to e5bc31c0-3223-8019-8629-1935188c7fe5. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 2, 7, 3, 1, 0, 2). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: rights.lean (3 observed, 0.89 expected, lift 3.38), energy.lean (4 observed, 2.33 expected, lift 1.72), families.lean (8 observed, 4.66 expected, lift 1.72). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.11; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.62. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 50.5% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. Nim — Charles L. Bouton, 1901; the Sprague–Grundy theorem — Roland Sprague, 1935 and Patrick M. Grundy, 1939 Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. bouton_two_heaps_lost_iff_xor_zero — (List.range N).all (fun a => (List.range N).all (fun b => isLost a b == (xorN a b == 0))) record
  2. bouton_lost_iff_heaps_equal — (List.range N).all (fun a => (List.range N).all (fun b => isLost a b == (a == b))) record
  3. lost_positions_are_exactly_the_diagonal — (((List.range N).flatMap (fun a => (List.range N).map (fun b => (a, b)))).filter (fun p => isLost p.1 p.2)).length = N record
  4. grundy_of_a_single_heap_is_its_size — (List.range N).all (fun n => grundy1 (n + 1) n == n) record
  5. grundy_of_two_heaps_is_the_xor — (List.range N).all (fun a => (List.range N).all (fun b => (xorN (grundy1 (a + 1) a) (grundy1 (b + 1) b)) == xorN a b)) record
  6. xor_is_its_own_inverse — (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN (xorN a b) b == a)) record
  7. xor_is_commutative — (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN a b == xorN b a)) record
  8. xor_zero_is_identity — (List.range 32).all (fun a => xorN a 0 == a) record
  9. the_nim_sum_is_a_gf2_vector_addition — (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN a b == xorN b a)) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => (List.range 16).all (fun c => xorN (xorN a b) c == xorN a (xorN b c)))) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a => (List.range 16).all (fun b => xorN (xorN a b) b == a)) ∧ (List.range 16).all (fun a => xorN a 0 == a) record
  10. bouton_holds_at_every_heap_size_to_six — (List.range 7).all (fun a => (List.range 7).all (fun b => isLost a b == (xorN a b == 0))) record
